dependencies.name: strings

candidate.name: str `in` operator, str.find
candidate.evidence: quote.go:50, quote.go:58, quote.go:77, unquote.go:40, unquote.go:88, unquote.go:117, unquote.go:140

dependencies.notes: Python's shlex (shlex.quote, shlex.split) was considered as a replacement for the whole package and rejected: it differs from the Go original. Probe on CPython 3.14.6: shlex.quote("don't") gives 'don'"'"'t' where Go Join gives don\'t; shlex.quote("foo*") gives 'foo*' where Go gives foo\*; shlex.split("text with\\\na newline") keeps the newline ('with\na') where Go elides it ('witha'); shlex raises one ValueError type where Go has three distinct errors. The package itself is the port.

dependencies.name: unicode/utf8

candidate.name: iteration over str code points
candidate.evidence: quote.go:48, unquote.go:39, unquote.go:50, unquote.go:74, unquote.go:105, unquote.go:130, unquote.go:138

dependencies.notes: Python str holds code points, so decoding is implicit. Go strings can hold invalid UTF-8, which DecodeRuneInString reads as U+FFFD width 1 and the code copies through as raw bytes; a Python str API cannot receive those bytes. This is a contract scope question (str-only API), not a dependency gap.
